determinism.method: The release was cut on a base read two ways (the manifest at HEAD and an SSM md5 walk of the host) and the ask's bytes were checked against the sha256 the GO names, so the halves demonstrably cover these bytes. The grant was applied targeted with a pre-act existence control and an IAM read-back. The refusal arm counts reads on FOUR module clients, because each module builds its own Scope client and a guard on the shared seam alone would have left three unguarded while reporting a clean zero. The probe arguments were derived from the host's own catalog at call time, because five of the six tools require an argument whose valid values are not constants.

mutant.description: The order names no mutant. FOUR negative arms stand in its place, each one a read that must come out DIFFERENTLY for the matching positive read to mean anything. (a) blob identity, paired with a file that must differ. (b) the naming clause, graded twice on the same diff with one input changed. (c) the host walk, bracketed so a truncated read cannot pass as complete. (d) the refusal guard, which RAISES on any attribute access so a read on a refusal path both counts and fails loudly rather than passing silently -- and it is installed on FOUR module clients, because one guard on the shared seam would have left three modules unguarded while still reporting a clean zero.

(4) THE REFUSAL GUARD raises on any attribute access, so a read on a refusal path both counts AND fails loudly rather than passing silently.

NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S144: the CTO half's condition 2 could not be met in its literal form. The S3PREFIX clause derives the committing project from the staged paths and a release commit stages release files only, by the order's own bound, so the two rules are jointly unsatisfiable on that commit. Three readings were handed to the CTO rather than the one that let this seat proceed; it ruled (msg 34411) the trunk ENFORCE grade plus a blob-identity read satisfies it.
